text:
rachael_sales: Heads-up 10: MerchantOne is moving to a signed commit. They want an operational pack: sustained 5k RPS for marketing windows, 2x short bursts, 200ms p95 SLA. Also asked for burst-credit pricing and a security questionnaire response. Can eng confirm resource plan + suggested autoscale rules?

jim_ops: Congrats! Quick baseline question: is the 5k RPS for single-turn or multi-turn sessions? and average response length?

rachel_sales: Mostly single-turn chat with ~400 token context on avg, occasional 2-3 turn flows. Reranks are rare (~5%).

own_infra: With seq ~400 and constraining batching latency to keep p95 under 200ms, practical throughput is ~750 rps per A100-equiv GPU when we cap queueing at 25ms. For sustained 5k RPS I'd size reserved slab at 7 GPUs. For headroom during 2x bursts, add a 5-GPU burst pool (prefer spot-backed).

deepa_se: Spot for bursts is OK but we should offer two burst profiles to customer: (A) cheaper spot-burst with quantized fallback and (B) premium reserved-burst (on-demand) with hard SLA. They usually pick A but legal asked for fallback guarantees.

kai_prod: Important: with KV cache warmed, effective per-GPU rps rises ~20-30%. Recommend preheat windows and a warming policy: preheat start 10m before campaign.

jim_ops: Autoscale proposal: monitor 30s RPS moving average, trigger scale up when >85% of reserved capacity for 60s, cooldown 90s, allow burst pool until a max of (reserved + burst) then apply 429s. Fallback policy: if spot eviction occurs, route overflow to quantized-8bit model (same checkpoints) and notify customer webhook.

deepa_se: Also note we should pin model commit SHA for Dedicated customers. Add a model-variant matrix to contract: baseline (full-precision), fallback (8-bit quantized), degraded (smaller model) with deterministic latency profiles.

own_infra: Pricing sketch for commercial: reserved 7 GPUs @ $X/month + burst credits priced per-GPU-hour. For draft commercial we can show two options: 1) conservative: 7 reserved + 5 reserved burst (higher cost, stronger SLA) 2) hybrid: 7 reserved + 5 spot burst credits (cheaper, documented eviction fallback).

rachel_sales: Legal asked for exact SLA language for failures during a burst. Can someone draft a short paragraph we can insert to the MSA?

jim_ops: Draft SLA blurb: "Redwood will provision reserved capacity as agreed. For transient burst capacity requested via burst credits, Redwood will use best-effort provisioning. If burst capacity cannot be provisioned within 120 seconds, Redwood will attempt an automated fallback to a quantized model variant. If capacity remains constrained, excess requests will be met with HTTP 429 responses; credits will apply as defined in the contract."

deepa_se: Add operational runbook steps: detect spike -> check KV warm metric -> if cold then kick preheat job -> route traffic to fallback if preheat fails -> escalate to oncall. We should attach a preheat curl example in the runbook.

own_infra: Preheat sample (curl): `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.example/v1/preheat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"job":"kv_warm","model":"merchantone-chat-v1","start_in":"10m","duration_mins":15}'`

rachel_sales: Security questionnaire items: MerchantOne needs confirmation for: a) CMEK/KMS support, b) VPC peering, c) audit log retention 1 year, d) SOC2 addendum. Any blockers?

deepa_se: No blockers. Private deployments support CMEK via customer KMS (we'll need key alias and IAM role). VPC peering available. Audit logs can be exported to their S3 or SIEM, retention configurable. SOC2 addendum: legal needs ~5 business days. I'll prepare a checklist doc.

kai_prod: Observability: propose a per-tenant dashboard with token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, coldstart rate, and KV cache hit ratio. Set alerts: p95 > 200ms for 2 consecutive 5-min windows -> page oncall + open incident link.

rachel_sales: Any per-route throttling recommendation? MerchantOne asked about graceful degradation instead of 429s?
